analysis:
The only changed content in this batch is a documentation-only addition to docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 1561-1569 per file_changes). It describes how LocalTokenizerBridge.decode releases trailing `<0xHH>` byte-fallback tokens and how DetokenizerV2 holds back U+FFFD. The two supplied units (head lines 420-1216) are unchanged surrounding text: the Nemotron Super and GLM5Next serving, memory admission, prefix-cache and SSD checkpoint documentation. Neither unit contains the changed hunk. I did not see the changed lines directly, so my read of them rests on the patch excerpt.

Security relevance: no code, config, authorization, attestation, encryption, cache-scope or billing behavior changes in this batch. The unchanged text agrees with T-041: durable checkpoints are encrypted under the provider cache root, partitioned by authenticated cache scope, and off without a scope. It also records that the SSD tier is the default and that DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1 selects the resident bank, which matches the cache-related threat posture. The documented tokenizer behavior is a correctness or availability detail on output text, not a trust-boundary change. No threat assumptions are invalidated, and I do not see a need to update the threat model.

Remaining questions: the actual LocalTokenizerLoader.swift implementation, if changed in another batch, should be checked for the decoding behavior the doc describes. For example, it should not cause unbounded buffering or leak plaintext through any path other than the encrypted response channel. That source is outside this batch, so I make no claim about it.
